mechanics.name: Plunderer's Instinct
mechanics.currentEffect: You see the Auras of Chests and Items. You unlock Chests 150/175/200% faster. Whenever you unlock a Chest, you are 50% more likely to find an Item of higher rarity.
activation: Unlock a Chest for the speed and higher-rarity Item effects.
Ends/deactivates when: The speed and rarity effects apply to Chest unlocking; the 10.2.0 notes do not extend the rarity trigger to rummaging.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (10.2.0): Removed the 32/48/64-metre Aura limit, added 150/175/200% faster Chest unlocking, and tied the 50% higher-rarity Item chance to Chest unlocking.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: See Chests and Items without the former range limit, open Chests dramatically faster, and improve the chance of a higher-rarity Item when unlocking one.
specialInteractions: The former 32/48/64-metre Aura range was removed.
The higher-rarity chance is tied to unlocking a Chest.

editorial.summary: See Chests and dropped Items without the old range limit, open Chests up to 200% faster, and improve higher-rarity Item odds by 50%.
useCases: Locate every relevant chest/item resource quickly.
Open Chests fast enough that a loot detour costs far less time than before.
Drive Appraisal, Ace in the Hole, Pharmacy, and other chest builds.
counters: Chest value competes with generator time.
A strong brought Item can make the whole chest economy unnecessary.
pros: 10.2 removed the old Aura range restriction.
Higher-rarity chance improves the average Item roll.
cons: Cannot guarantee the Item category you need.
Low value if the team already entered with premium Items.
analysis: Plunderer’s Instinct is another 10.2 perk that should not inherit its old reputation. The Aura range restriction is gone and Chest opening can be 200% faster at Tier III, substantially reducing the time cost of the entire loot strategy.
The 50% higher-rarity modifier remains, so the perk now combines map-wide resource information, dramatically faster acquisition, and better average quality in one slot.
That does not make Chests the main objective. Random Items still have to repay travel and interaction time, and a lobby that already brought strong equipment has less reason to loot.
The live version deserves a meaningful promotion among specialist perks. It is still a chest perk, but it is finally an extremely efficient chest perk.
editorial.verdict: A serious chest-build perk after 10.2. Global resource information and 200% faster opening make looting far less embarrassing to the team’s generator clock.
